Mark the student's response to a question from the 2019 NSW HSC Ancient History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Question 2 [8 marks]: Explain the ethical issues facing archaeologists who study Pompeii and Herculaneum. Support your response using evidence from Source B and other relevant sources.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 8):
7–8 marks: Provides a well-developed and accurate explanation about the ethical issues facing archaeologists who study Pompeii and Herculaneum | Supports response using Source B and other relevant sources | Uses historical terms and concepts appropriately
5–6 marks: Provides a sound explanation about the ethical issues facing archaeologists who study Pompeii and Herculaneum | Refers to Source B and other relevant sources | Uses historical terms and concepts appropriately
3–4 marks: Provides some explanation about the ethical issues facing archaeologists who study Pompeii and Herculaneum | Refers to Source B | May use historical terms and concepts
1–2 marks: Makes general statements relevant to the question | May refer to Source B


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Display of human/animal remains: for example, skeletons in Herculaneum boatshed
• Study of human/animal remains: for example, Bisel’s and/or Lazer’s approach and conclusions
• Reconstruction: for example, misleading interpretations
• Conservation: for example, appropriate materials, purpose, question of further excavation
• Tourism: inclusion of plaster casts in travelling exhibitions; beneficial vs negative impact.
• Custodianship and management of the site.
